PC: Formulate acute and long-term treatment plans.
Properly position patient to minimize risk of syncope – supine or semi-supine in dental chair.
Emergency management – discuss airway protection, lower head, raise feet. With delayed recovery, call 911.

Prevention – provide comfortable environment, encourage patient to eat prior to visit and/or maintain adequate hydration $( O J )$ , minimize stress to patient, conduct thorough pre-procedure assess of patient medical history.
MK: Recognize and interpret pressure and EKG traces on clinical monitors.
Define the cardiac rate and rhythm.
Measure and analyze the cardiac output.
Recognize the effect of pain /fear associated with local anesthesia and its relationship to neurogenic shock.
List the signs and symptoms of neurogenic shock.
Determine the risk factors to minimize risks.
Identify the most critical problem of the patient based on pt’s clinical information, chief complaints, & the student’s own physical assessment and verbalize “WHY”.
SBP: Verbalize necessary referrals for this patient, assuming more care is needed.
Delegate tasks to other healthcare members (oral surgeon extraction under sedation)
